title: Machine-learning workflow guides Na-doped RuO2 for durable acidic water electrolysis
summary: An adaptive machine-learning workflow described potential-dependent evolution of the RuO2(110) surface, identifying an active state with distorted RuO5 units that converts to inert RuO4 units at higher potential. It yielded an inverse volcano-type doping rule, in which the dopant-oxygen bond strength should differ markedly from Ru-O. Applying the rule, the authors predicted and experimentally confirmed that Na stabilizes RuO2 in its active state: Na-RuO2 operated for over 1800 h in acidic oxygen evolution without degradation and showed durability in PEM electrolysis. Only one dopant is reported as confirmed in the abstract.
ai_technology: Adaptive machine-learning workflow for surface evolution of RuO2(110) and doping design
